item.title: Presidential Message on Fire Prevention Week
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on Fire Prevention WeekThe White HouseOctober 5, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on Fire Prevention WeekThe White HouseOctober 5, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on Fire Prevention WeekThe White HouseOctober 5, 2026
Briefings & Statements
The White HouseOctober 5, 2026
During Fire Prevention Week, my Administration honors the memory of America’s courageous firefighters and first responders for their extraordinary service and sacrifice. We are reaffirming our commitment to strengthening fire prevention and emergency response across the Nation. I encourage every American to take simple steps to protect their homes, families, and communities from preventable fires.
Fire safety begins at home. Every family can take precautions to prevent fires, and to better protect themselves and their loved ones. These can include mapping out a home escape plan, testing smoke and carbon monoxide alarms every month, replacing the worn wiring and overloaded outlets that spark so many household fires, or practicing safe charging habits that minimize the potential of fires from ubiquitous electronic devices. These commonsense steps can save lives by preventing fire or by ensuring families are prepared in the event of an emergency.
My Administration remains committed to protecting American lives from the threat of fires and improving our country’s ability to prevent and respond to them. Last year, I signed an Executive Order to streamline Federal wildfire response, strengthen local preparedness, and put modern technology to work detecting and fighting fires. We are also working to establish the United States Wildland Fire Service to better coordinate Federal wildfire programs and respond more effectively when fires break out.
This week, we also honor America’s extraordinary firefighters, first responders, emergency personnel, and volunteers who selflessly respond whenever the alarm sounds. Their determination to aid fellow Americans in distress embodies the highest American ideals of heroism, courage, and service to others. Together, we recommit to preventing fires, protecting our communities, and building a Nation more prepared, more ready, and more resilient than ever before.

item.title: Presidential Message on Child Health Day
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on Child Health DayThe White HouseOctober 5, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on Child Health DayThe White HouseOctober 5, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on Child Health DayThe White HouseOctober 5, 2026
Briefings & Statements
The White HouseOctober 5, 2026
This Child Health Day, we renew our commitment to ensure the health and well-being of America’s children – our Nation’s future – so that they may live full, lasting, and happy lives free from the burden of health concerns.
As our children grow, we must protect their health and give them every opportunity to thrive. American children now face chronic health conditions and serious medical issues at rates far higher than in previous generations. With little explanation, we have witnessed sharp rises in the prevalence of obesity, diabetes, severe allergies, autism, autoimmune diseases, and mental health challenges such as anxiety and depression in our Nation’s youth. As President, I have a solemn duty to safeguard the health of the coming generation, and I will not rest until these conditions are understood and defeated and every child in America can grow up strong and whole.
For this reason, my Administration is confronting the chronic health crisis plaguing our Nation’s most vulnerable citizens by reversing the failed policies that have fueled America’s childhood disease epidemic and ensuring parents are informed with the Gold Standard Science to make the decisions for their children. Through the Make Our Children Healthy Again Strategy—an initiative launched by the Make America Healthy Again Commission—we have taken over 120 specific actions to halt the rise in childhood chronic diseases and discover the root causes of serious medical conditions by improving preventative care, getting artificial dyes out of our food, accelerating breakthroughs and cures, and encouraging physical activity and limited screen time for children.
While more work remains to fully reverse these concerning trends, in just the first year of my Administration, we experienced the lowest death rate in recorded in our country’s history. Our Nation’s future relies upon the health and leadership of the next generation, which is why I remain committed to ensuring that Americans and their children receive the best medical advice to keep them healthy and the best care in the world if they do get sick. Under my leadership, we are delivering a healthcare system that restores trust and truly puts the health of children and families first, and together, we will make American children healthy again for generations to come.

item.title: Presidential Message on German American Day
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on German American DayThe White HouseOctober 6, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on German American DayThe White HouseOctober 6, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on German American DayThe White HouseOctober 6, 2026
Briefings & Statements
The White HouseOctober 6, 2026
The German American story began on October 6, 1683, when 13 families from Krefeld, after braving the Atlantic in search of opportunity, landed on our shores and soon founded Germantown, Pennsylvania—the first permanent German settlement in America.
In the centuries since, German Americans have farmed the fields of our heartland and powered the industries that turned our young country into the mightiest economic powerhouse in the world.Their sons and daughters have defended American freedom in every era, serving valiantly in both World Wars and standing watch through the long struggle against communism during the Cold War. In our own time, their descendants continuetoserve in our Armed Forces, work the factories and family farms that sustain our Nation, and lead the businesses and communities that keep the American Dream alive for all of our citizens.
This spirit endures in the long-standing relationship between the United States and Germany—a relationship sustained by our mutual respect, and a shared desire for peace and prosperity. As President, I have led a historic renewal of the NATO alliance, securing a historic commitment from our NATO allies to increase their investment in our common defense. Since that historic summit in The Hague last year, Germany has taken bold steps toward the realization of a stronger, more balanced NATO. The impact of this commitment will be felt beyond Europe, as billions of dollars in new investments strengthen the transatlantic defense industrial base and create thousands of high-paying jobs for American workers.
Today, we give thanks for the generations of German Americans whose labor and love of liberty helped make the United States the greatest Nation on Earth. Their story is woven into the fabric of America, and together, we commit ourselves to building on this legacy to create an even brighter, more prosperous future for all Americans.

The White HouseOctober 7, 2026
On Wednesday, October 7, 2026, the President signed into law:
H.R. 5345, the “Improving Social Security’s Service to Victims of Identity Theft Act,” which establishes a single point of contact at the Social Security Administration for individuals whose Social Security Number has been misused or whose Social Security card has been lost; and
S. 766, the “Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act of 2025,” which requires an annual report on federally-funded projects that are more than 5 years behind schedule or more than $1 billion over the original cost estimate.

item.title: Presidential Message on Leif Erikson Day
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on Leif Erikson DayThe White HouseOctober 9, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on Leif Erikson DayThe White HouseOctober 9, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on Leif Erikson DayThe White HouseOctober 9, 2026
Briefings & Statements
The White HouseOctober 9, 2026
Half a millennium before legendary American hero Christopher Columbus set foot in the New World, Norse explorer Leif Erikson made history as the first European to arrive on the North American continent. This Leif Erikson Day, we celebrate his exceptional legacy of bravery, daring, and exploration as we build upon our extraordinary relationships with our Nordic partners and open a glorious new chapter in America’s Arctic story.
Born in 970, Leif Erikson developed a love for exploration and adventure that he would carry through his entire life, a calling that would change the world for centuries to come. His steadfast Christian faith gave him the conviction to sail into the unknown, voyaging over 1,800 miles across the Atlantic with a small crew of 35 men and overcoming raging winds, crashing waves, and crippling storms to reach the shores of L’Anse aux Meadows in northern Newfoundland, Canada—the land he named “Vinland.” In doing so, he opened the door between two worlds and proved that no ocean could hold back the course of discovery—the same daring spirit that would one day build the greatest Nation on Earth.
A millennium later, that resolve lives on in America’s outstanding relationships with Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden—nations bound to us by adventure, fortitude, and faith in Almighty God. Nowhere is that bond stronger today than in Greenland, where Lief Erikson once led a settlement of his own and where my Administration has now secured Greenland’s future as a bastion for U.S. security and transatlantic defense.
Last month, I entered into a historic agreement with Denmark and Greenland that gives the United States permanent control over security in Greenland, guaranteeing our ability to safeguard America and our allies for all time. In concluding this agreement, I did what no President in the last 100 years was willing to do—I permanently recognized Greenland as an essential national security partner and made the Arctic a pillar of American strength once again. For centuries to come, Americans will be safer, our Arctic frontier will be stronger, and our bond with the Nordic peoples will be closer than ever before.
As we reflect on the enduring legacy of Leif Erikson, we recognize his rightful place in our glorious American story, we honor the millions of Nordic Americans whose contributions have shaped the life of our Nation, and we commit to carrying the spirit of his marvelous discovery boldly into America’s next chapter of exploration, friendship, and greatness.

item.title: Presidential Message on General Pulaski Memorial Day
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on General Pulaski Memorial DayThe White HouseOctober 11, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on General Pulaski Memorial DayThe White HouseOctober 11, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on General Pulaski Memorial DayThe White HouseOctober 11, 2026
Briefings & Statements
The White HouseOctober 11, 2026
Today, we honor the heroic life and legacy of Brigadier General Casimir Pulaski—a son of Poland turned American warrior, a father of Independence, and a martyr of Liberty, whose courage breathed life into the Continental Army, advancing the sacred cause of freedom during the Revolutionary War.
Born in Warsaw, Poland, in 1745, Casimir Pulaski proved himself to be a battle-hardened patriot from an early age, courageously fighting to defend the freedom of his countrymen against Russian aggression. Recognizing his extraordinary military skill, fearless spirit, and profound devotion to liberty, Benjamin Franklin recruited him to cross the Atlantic Ocean and join the Continental Army’s righteous fight for Independence.
Without hesitation, Pulaski arrived on our shores in the summer of 1777 and, within weeks, displayed his bravery and tactical expertise at the Battle of Brandywine against the might of the British Empire. When American lines collapsed under a devastating British flanking attack, threatening the fate of our young Republic, Pulaski rose to the call of history and gathered a small band of horsemen to lead a defiant charge against the British, allowing George Washington and his men to escape death and retreat to safety.
In the year following, Pulaski transformed a ragtag cavalry into a unified, disciplined fighting force capable of defeating the mightiest army in the world, earning him the title “Father of the American Cavalry.” In October 1779, he gave his life for the cause of liberty while leading a cavalry charge during the Siege of Savannah—etching his name forever into the heart of America.
Pulaski’s legacy of sacrifice, courage, and strength is a testament to the unyielding fortitude of the Polish people. From overcoming the brutal despotism of Nazi Germany to defeating the devastating tyranny of communism, they have shown the world the unstoppable power of freedom and the unbreakable resolve of the human spirit, so magnificently embodied in the life and legacy of General Casimir Pulaski. As I proudly declared in Warsaw during my first term, the United States is immeasurably enriched by the contributions of Polish Americans, who have defended our freedom and made our Nation greater, stronger, and more prosperous. Bound by our shared love of liberty, the United States and Poland enjoy a steadfast bond and friendship that my Administration is continuing to strengthen.
As we pay tribute to a remarkable warrior who gave his life for our young Republic, we remember General Pulaski for his battlefield brilliance and the unwavering devotion to freedom that burned within him until his very last breath. Inspired by his bravery and patriotism, may we continue to cherish, defend, and carry forward the sacred flame of liberty that he and generations of Americans shed their blood to preserve.

item.title: First Lady Melania Trump Launches 2027 Presidential SI Challenge and Establishes First Lady Seal of SI Readiness
item.description:

Office of the First Lady
The White HouseOctober 13, 2026
First Lady Melania Trump launched her 2027 Presidential Super Intelligence (SI) Challenge and established a new First Lady Seal of SI Readiness—inviting K-12 students, educators, and schools across America to participate in the nationwide initiative.
“America’s next groundbreaking idea is already sitting in a classroom,” said Mrs. Trump. “We must give our children the knowledge, tools, and opportunities to bring those ideas to life.”
Following the success of the inaugural Challenge earlier this year, which engaged more than 20,000 students from all 50 states and U.S. schools around the world, the 2027 Presidential SI Challenge will continue to give students the opportunity to use SI to dream, build, and develop solutions to real-world challenges.
“America’s future security, prosperity, and global leadership depend on our next generation. Building on last year’s success, the 2027 Presidential Super Intelligence Challenge will empower our children to lead the world,” said First Lady Melania Trump.
New this year, all participating schools will have the opportunity to earn the First Lady Seal of SI Readiness by completing and submitting evidence of a rigorous set of milestones focused on SI readiness. The Seal recognizes schools that are taking meaningful steps to prepare students and educators to understand, use, and responsibly engage with super intelligence.
The Presidential SI Challenge will continue its project-based competition, encouraging students to explore super intelligence through creative and innovative projects that address challenges in their schools, communities, and beyond. To watch First Lady Melania Trump’s launch video, to learn more, and to sign up for the Challenge, please visitSI.Gov.

item.title: Presidential Message on the Birthday of the United States Navy
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on the Birthday of the United States NavyThe White HouseOctober 13, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on the Birthday of the United States NavyThe White HouseOctober 13, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on the Birthday of the United States NavyThe White HouseOctober 13, 2026
Briefings & Statements
The White HouseOctober 13, 2026
For over 250 years, American sailors have defended our Nation upon the seas, forging the most lethal Navy in the history of the world. Today, on the birthday of the United States Navy, Icelebrate this incredible milestone with our active duty and reserve sailors, past and present, whose unparalleled expertise and extraordinary devotion to duty in times of war and peace have carried our Navy to these unrivaled heights.
On October 13, 1775, our Navy was formally established when the Second Continental Congress authorized a pair of armed vessels to sail against the mighty British Empire, intercept enemy supply lines, and defend the cause of American liberty at sea during the Revolutionary War. Since its humble beginnings, the Navy has grown into the most formidable seafaring force the world has ever known.
Today’s sailors are part of a storied legacy of maritime supremacy that has safeguarded our sovereignty in every major conflict since. Our warships are unmistakable symbols of American military might, but the most sophisticated, state-of-the-art fleet is nothing without the elite men and women who carry out every mission at home and abroad with unwavering resolve and professionalism. In home ports and on carrier decks, submarine patrols, and distant oceans, our sailor stand watch around the clock, deterring aggression, keeping the world’s great sea lanes open and free, and carrying American strength to every corner of the globe. Their skill and sacrifice keep our Republic safe and secure in the blessings of liberty, earning the everlasting gratitude of the American People.
As President, I am rebuilding our incredible Navy and restoring the mighty American shipbuilding industry that sustains it, ensuring our fleet is prepared to meet every challenge of our age. Since returning to office, my Administration has secured over $150 billion in investments to usher in the Golden Age of American shipbuilding. In August, I was proud to sign a National Security Presidential Memorandum that directs the Department of War to pursue more direct investments in the American shipbuilding industrial base, expanding our capacity to build warships and creating good-paying jobs for American workers. The Memorandum further directs the Secretary of War to establish a fifth Naval shipyard, the first in more than eight decades, to increase our Nation’s submarine and aircraft carrier repair capacity. Just last week we saw the fruit of those actions as construction began on the largest new shipyard in the United States since World War II, which will build the next generation of American submarines. Under my leadership, our Navy will be bigger, better, and stronger than ever before.
Since the dawn of our glorious Republic, generation after generation of valiant sailors have answered the Navy’s stern call for “faith, courage, service true, with honor over all.” Today, the First Lady joins me in saluting over two and a half centuries of American dominance upon the seas and honor the heroes who secure the freedom and safety of the American People.

item.title: Presidential Message on the Birthday of President Dwight D. Eisenhower
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on the Birthday of President Dwight D. EisenhowerThe White HouseOctober 14, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on the Birthday of President Dwight D. EisenhowerThe White HouseOctober 14, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on the Birthday of President Dwight D. EisenhowerThe White HouseOctober 14, 2026
Briefings & Statements
The White HouseOctober 14, 2026
On this day, we mark the 136th birthday of President Dwight David Eisenhower—a visionary leader, respected warrior, distinguished statesman, and noble public servant. In command of great armies and in the White House, he met every trial with steadiness, courage, and resolve, earning the enduring trust of the American People and the lasting gratitude of the free world.
Born in Denison, Texas, and raised in Abilene, Kansas, President Eisenhower began his legendary life of service to our great Nation as a graduate of West Point. His stellar military career spanned nearly four decades and included appointments such as the Supreme Commander of the Allied Expeditionary Force during World War II, during which he orchestrated the historic D-Day Invasion of Normandy, and as NATO’s first Supreme Allied Commander Europe. In his first bid for the Presidency in 1952, the celebrated general and political outsider was elected in a landslide victory. After four years, Americans still liked “Ike” and handed him another decisive win in the 1956 election.
Eisenhower’s tenure in the White House was marked by peace, growth, economic prosperity, and a remarkable record of foreign and domestic accomplishments. He negotiated an armistice in the Korean War, signed the Civil Rights Act of 1957, created the National Aeronautics and Space Administration and the Small Business Administration, and championed the Interstate Highway System, which connected communities across our country and boosted American commerce. Eisenhower’s commitment to military might and the preservation of our birthright of freedom is reflected in the cautionary words from his 1953 Inaugural Address: “History does not long entrust the care of freedom to the weak or the timid.”
My Administration is proudly advancing the ideals that shaped Eisenhower’s Presidency, including economic prosperity, a strong national defense, secure borders, an unwavering commitment to peace through strength, and the tireless pursuit of American exceptionalism. Like President Eisenhower, I believe lasting peace is secured only through unquestioned American strength, and my Administration is rebuilding our military into the most powerful fighting force on Earth. We are upholding the law and order he championed, making our streets and communities safe again, igniting an economic boom unlike anything our country has ever seen, and renewing the strength and spirit of American life at every turn. More than seven decades later, Eisenhower’s example continues to guide our Nation as we restore the peace, prosperity, and confidence that defined his era and usher in a new Golden Age for the American People.
As we commemorate the birthday of our 34th Commander in Chief, we honor the extraordinary life and legacy of this patriot, hero, and American icon, whose devotion to duty and country will inspire Americans for generations to come.
Happy Birthday, President Eisenhower!
